mcqs.question: What does inertia of motion refer to?

options.A: The tendency of a moving object to continue moving at the same speed in the same direction unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.
options.B: The tendency of a moving object to stop automatically after a short time.
options.C: The tendency of a stationary object to start moving on its own.
options.D: The tendency of an object to change its shape while moving.

mcqs.answer: The tendency of a moving object to continue moving at the same speed in the same direction unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion is the property that a body in motion remains in motion with the same speed and direction unless a net external force acts on it. Option A states this correctly; the other options describe unrelated or incorrect ideas.

mcqs.question: Inertia of direction means that:

options.A: An object resists any change in its state of rest.
options.B: An object resists any change in the direction of its motion.
options.C: An object resists any change in its speed only.
options.D: An object resists any change in its shape.

mcqs.answer: An object resists any change in the direction of its motion.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of direction is the aspect of inertia that prevents a moving object from changing its line of motion unless a force acts perpendicular to its motion. Option B captures this; the other options refer to different aspects of inertia or unrelated properties.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly states Newton's first law of motion?

options.A: An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion continues in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.B: An object will accelerate in the direction of the applied force regardless of its mass.
options.C: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
options.D: The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to its mass.

mcqs.answer: An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion continues in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by a net external force.
mcqs.explanation: Newton's first law (law of inertia) is exactly described in option A. Option B mixes concepts from the second law, option C describes the third law, and option D is the quantitative form of the second law.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an everyday example that illustrates Newton's first law of motion?

options.A: A book sliding on a perfectly frictionless table continues forever.
options.B: A car accelerates forward when you press the gas pedal.
options.C: A ball rolling on a floor eventually comes to rest because of friction.
options.D: A skydiver reaches a constant speed after falling for a while.

mcqs.answer: A ball rolling on a floor eventually comes to rest because of friction.
mcqs.explanation: The ball keeps moving at constant speed until an unbalanced external force (friction) acts, demonstrating that motion persists without net force. Option C shows this clearly. Option A is idealized and not everyday; B and D involve net forces causing acceleration or reaching terminal velocity, not the pure statement of inertia.

mcqs.question: Inertia can be best defined as:

options.A: The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion.
options.B: The force required to start moving a stationary object.
options.C: The speed at which an object moves.
options.D: The product of mass and acceleration.

mcqs.answer: The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is a property of matter that makes it resist changes in its motion, whether at rest or moving. Option A states this definition precisely. Option B confuses inertia with the applied force, C describes speed, and D is Newton's second law.

mcqs.question: A book is lying undisturbed on a table. It remains there until you push it. Which concept best explains this behavior?
mcqs.explanation: The book stays at rest because of inertia of rest—it resists a change from rest to motion until an external force (your push) acts. Option B is correct; the other options refer to different aspects of inertia that are not relevant here.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about inertia of motion is FALSE?

options.A: A moving object will eventually stop even if no external force acts on it.
options.B: A moving object will continue moving at constant velocity unless acted upon by an external force.
options.C: The amount of inertia depends on the object's mass.
options.D: Inertia is an inherent property of matter.

mcqs.answer: A moving object will eventually stop even if no external force acts on it.
mcqs.explanation: According to Newton's first law, a moving object does not stop on its own; it needs an external unbalanced force (like friction). Therefore, statement A is false. Statements B, C, and D correctly describe inertia of motion.

mcqs.question: A car is traveling north at a constant speed. The driver suddenly turns the steering wheel to head east. According to Newton's first law, which statement best describes what happens to the car's motion?

options.A: The car instantly changes direction to east without any force.
options.B: The car continues moving north until a lateral force changes its direction.
options.C: The car comes to a stop immediately.
options.D: The car's speed increases as it turns.

mcqs.answer: The car continues moving north until a lateral force changes its direction.
mcqs.explanation: Newton's first law states that an object maintains its state of motion (both speed and direction) unless acted upon by an external force. Turning the wheel applies a lateral force; until that force acts, the car would tend to keep moving north. Hence option B is correct. Options A, C, and D contradict the law.
